title: Multitask Deep Learning Model for Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis and Disease-Free Survival From Cytology Images in Bladder Cancer: A Multicenter Study With Pan-Cytology Validation.
summary: Accurate prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) and survival outcomes is crucial for personalized treatment in bladder cancer, yet remains clinically challenging. This study aimed to develop a Cytology-based multitask predictive Network (CytoNet) to simultaneously predict LNM and disease-free survival (DFS) in bladder cancer, and to evaluate its generalizability in cervical and thyroid cancers. This study included a multicenter cohort of 5273 patients, with bladder cancer (n = 1134), cervical cancer (n = 598), and thyroid cancer (n = 3541). CytoNet was constructed through a three-stage pipeline comprising self-supervised pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and multitask prediction. In bladder cancer, CytoNet achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.831-0.881 for LNM prediction and a C index of 0.680-0.710 for DFS prediction across all cohorts, outperforming single-task models and standard radiological assessments. In cervical cancer, CytoNet demonstrated robust performance for both LNM prediction (AUC 0.847-0.862) and DFS prediction (C index 0.690-0.709), while in thyroid cancer, it achieved an AUC of 0.819-0.855 for LNM prediction. In conclusion, CytoNet represents a reliable tool for predicting LNM and prognosis from cytopathology images across multiple cancer types, showing potential as a valuable adjunct to current clinical decision-making. Further prospective validation is warranted to assess its clinical utility.

title: From cytoreduction to precision oncology: evolution of ovarian cancer therapy.
summary: Ovarian cancer remains the most lethal gynecologic malignancy due to its asymptomatic progression, limited screening modalities, and late-stage diagnosis. Although initial responses to platinum-based chemotherapy are common, recurrence and multidrug resistance are nearly universal, necessitating a shift toward biomarker-guided, precision-based interventions. This review synthesizes current evidence on the evolving landscape of ovarian cancer treatment, with emphasis on molecular pathogenesis, histotype-specific vulnerabilities, and advances in therapeutic strategies. Focus is placed on the clinical integration of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-targeting agents, immune checkpoint inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates, alongside emerging platforms such as liquid biopsy, artificial intelligence-enhanced diagnostics, and histotype-driven targeted therapies. Translational insights from other malignancies were utilized to highlight future directions for ovarian cancer, including dual pathway targeting, immune and epigenetic modulation, and receptor-guided cytotoxic delivery. Collectively, these advances demonstrate how precision oncology is advancing ovarian cancer treatment, with the potential to improve survival outcomes while preserving quality of life.

title: [Clinical reasoning in the age of artificial intelligence: the urgent need for formal education].
summary: Clinical reasoning remains the cornerstone of medical practice, yet unlike anatomy or physiology, medical curricula rarely teach it explicitly. This omission has significant consequences, as diagnostic errors account for up to 15% of adverse events in healthcare. Theoretical models such as Dual Process Theory (System 1 intuitive vs. System 2 analytical reasoning), illness scripts, and metacognition highlight both the strengths and vulnerabilities of clinical cognition. The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into clinical practice intensifies the need for structured reasoning education. While large language models demonstrate impressive diagnostic capabilities, risks such as automation bias and AI confabulations threaten safe decision-making. Consequently, this review calls for a paradigm shift: clinical reasoning must become a formal, longitudinal core subject across all stages of medical education. In the AI era, clinical reasoning is not diminished; it is indispensable.

title: Replicability and Validity of a New Artificial-Intelligence Assessment of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder From Patient Language: A Sequential Evaluation With Model Preregistration.
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) shows promise in identifying psychopathology through language, but replicability in AI models remains challenging. We develop an AI-based language assessment of posttraumatic-stress-disorder (PTSD) severity and introduce the sequential evaluation with model preregistration to rigorously evaluate its validity and replicability. This design includes two phases: development with preregistration and evaluation. Data included development (N = 1,437) and prospective (N = 346) samples, in which participants described their lives during automated interviews. In the prospective sample, preregistered models correlated with PTSD CheckList scores (r = .38, p < .001) and converged with PTSD diagnosis (area under the curve [AUC] = .76; outperforming demographics and trauma exposures: AUC = .61, p < .01). We found that for each standard-deviation increase, mental-health-care expenditure rose by $696.50 (p < .001). Our preregistered PTSD model assessments are replicable in prospectively collected clinical data and showed external validity against expense criteria. With further development, such models can be used to screen for PTSD or monitor treatment response, especially in telehealth or automated interviews, in which deployment can be seamless.

title: Can Current Innovations in Diagnostic and Therapeutic Strategies Transform Gastroesophageal Cancer Care?
summary: Gastric and esophageal cancers pose major global health challenges due to high incidence, frequent late-stage diagnosis, and poor survival outcomes. This review synthesized current evidence on emerging technologies and innovative approaches shaping research and practice. We included studies that evaluated diagnostic imaging, endoscopic and surgical treatments, molecular biomarkers, staging, screening, and innovative therapeutic approaches in gastric and esophageal cancers. The review revealed notable demographic and geographic disparities in disease incidence and outcomes. Recent advancements in endoscopic techniques, imaging modalities, and staging systems have enhanced early detection and prognostic stratification. Intriguing findings include significant improvements in survival with HER2-targeted and immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapies, the ability of liquid biopsy to detect resistance mutations and monitor treatment efficacy in real time, and the use of patient-derived organoids to predict individualized responses. Additionally, artificial intelligence (AI) applications have reduced diagnostic variability, thereby refining therapeutic decision-making. Despite promising innovations, further validation of these emerging technologies is required. Integrating advanced imaging, biomarker-based treatments, and AI-driven tools into clinical practice holds the potential to optimize treatment strategies and improve survival outcomes in gastroesophageal cancers.

title: Atlas-assisted segment anything model for fetal brain MRI (FeTal-SAM).
summary: This paper presents FeTal-SAM, a novel adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) tailored for fetal brain MRI segmentation. Traditional deep learning methods often require large annotated datasets for a fixed set of labels, making them inflexible when clinical or research needs change. By integrating atlas-based prompts and foundation-model principles, FeTal-SAM addresses two key limitations in fetal brain MRI segmentation: (1) the need to retrain models for varying label definitions, and (2) the lack of insight into whether segmentations are driven by genuine image contrast or merely inferred by learned spatial priors. We leverage multi-atlas registration to generate spatially aligned label templates that serve as dense prompts, alongside a bounding-box prompt, for SAM's segmentation decoder. This strategy enables binary segmentation on a per-structure basis, which is subsequently fused to reconstruct the full 3D segmentation volumes. Evaluations on two datasets, the dHCP dataset and an in-house dataset demonstrate FeTal-SAM's robust performance across gestational ages. Notably, it achieves Dice scores comparable to state-of-the-art baselines which were trained for each dataset and label definition for well-contrasted structures like cortical plate and cerebellum, while maintaining the flexibility to segment anatomical structures that could be templated by compatible atlas image and label sample pairs. Although slightly lower accuracy is observed for subtle, low-contrast structures (e.g., hippocampus, amygdala), our results highlight FeTal-SAM's potential as a flexible atlas-conditioned segmentation framework without requiring a separately trained model for each supported parcellation. This method thus constitutes a promising step toward clinically adaptable fetal brain MRI analysis tools.

title: Multivariate-Activated DNA Logic Gate for Predicting Responses to Cisplatin-Based Chemotherapy.
summary: Cisplatin-based chemotherapy remains an attractive alternative for controlling advanced cancers. However, a subset of cancer patients exhibits resistance to cisplatin. Accurate and early prediction of individual responses to cisplatin treatment is critical to personalized medicine guidance. The development of an effective method to predict chemotherapy response in cancer patients still faces challenges. Based on extracellular lactate, a key indicator of cisplatin resistance, herein, we report a multivariate-activated DNA logic gate to achieve lactate imaging with high fidelity. This device is assembled by a PNA-peptide-PNA copolymer and a lactate-specific aptamer with a cell membrane-anchoring aptamer module. It operates in response to the matrix metalloproteinase in the tumor microenvironment (TME) after the device anchors to nucleolin; thereby, the liberated aptamer binds to lactate through structure switching, achieving "off-on" fluorescence imaging. Additionally, imaging characteristics in combination with the Logistic Regression algorithm enable noninvasive prediction of cancer responses to cisplatin-based chemotherapy. In 90 cisplatin-resistant tumor-bearing mice, this detection model effectively identifies 77 of the 90 samples, showing a satisfactory accuracy of 85.6%. We further monitor the lactate level decreases in the TME using our method after the drug-resistant tumor-bearing mice treatment by stiripentol and successfully predict the enhancement of the therapeutic effect and the extension of the survival period. This study highlights the combined power of the DNA logic gate and machine learning for the analysis of lactate, paving the way for clinical cisplatin resistance detection and facilitating the formulation of personalized medicine guidance.

title: Protective effects of testosterone replacement therapy on brain tumor outcomes: The Mayo Clinic experience.
summary: Biological sex and endocrine signaling influence cancer biology, immune response, and therapeutic outcomes. Recent evidence suggests that testosterone signaling may exert brain-context-dependent protective effects in glioblastoma (GBM) through the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, reduced glucocorticoid-mediated immune suppression, and altered tumor-immune interactions. We assessed whether testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) exposure was associated with survival in solid tumor central nervous system (CNS) metastases and glioblastoma (GBM, IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4), settings in which post-diagnosis survival and TRT timing can be clinically defined. We performed a retrospective Mayo Clinic cohort study of adult patients with molecularly confirmed GBM and solid tumor CNS metastases confirmed from neuroimaging reports using large language model-assisted adjudication. TRT exposure was defined by testosterone-specific prescription evidence within prespecified peri-diagnostic windows. Overall survival was evaluated using propensity score-matched Cox models, 24-month administratively censored Cox models, time-dependent Cox sensitivity analyses, and 24-month restricted mean survival time. In the pooled solid tumor CNS metastasis cohort, TRT exposure was associated with improved overall survival after propensity score matching (HR 0.80, 95% CI, 0.65-0.98, P = .029) and a 3.22-month improvement in 24-month restricted mean survival time. In GBM, TRT exposure was similarly associated with improved overall survival after propensity score matching (HR 0.38, 95% CI, 0.14-0.98, P = .046) and a 5.81-month improvement in 24-month restricted mean survival time. TRT exposure was associated with improved survival in CNS metastases and glioblastoma. These hypothesis-generating findings support prospective studies incorporating TRT timing, hormone levels, corticosteroid exposure, immune correlates, and tumor-specific stratification.

title: Integrating emerging preservation strategies in cardiac transplantation: From nanotherapeutic frontiers to clinical translation.
summary: Hypothermic preservation remains a critical bottleneck in heart transplantation, primarily due to the exacerbation of ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and tightly restricted organ viability windows. Addressing this global clinical crisis requires a departure from traditional monotherapies. This review critically appraises-rather than merely synthesizes-three multidisciplinary advancements: (1) preservation solutions supplemented with nanotherapeutics, with explicit distinction between proof-of-concept, small-animal, and clinically translatable evidence; (2) technological transitions from static cold storage (SCS) to ex vivo heart perfusion (EVHP) and nanowarming-assisted cryopreservation; and (3) bioactive compounds derived from Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), evaluated through a SWOT framework that acknowledges phytochemical variability and the paucity of clinical transplantation data. We further examine the emerging-but currently nascent and largely speculative---role of artificial intelligence in perfusion decision support. We emphasize that these three domains are not evidentially equivalent: perfusion technology is clinically implemented, pharmacological and nanotherapeutic adjuncts remain predominantly preclinical, and AI applications in cardiac preservation are currently confined to retrospective outcome modelling, with no published closed-loop perfusion control in clinical practice.

It outlines applications for AI in numerous areas, including adaptive learning, procedural simulation, and competency-based assessment. Additionally, the authors discuss the inherent issues with this technology, including deskilling, algorithmic bias, and data opacity. Ultimately, the article argues for a value-based, ethical implementation strategy rooted in continuous quality improvement, ensuring that AI integration augments human judgment and advances safe, equitable patient care.

title: Simulation-Based Training in Anesthesiology.
summary: Simulation-based training is now an essential element of anesthesiology education, mandated by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education and incorporated into Maintenance of Certification in Anesthesia requirements. This review provides a comprehensive examination of simulation, ranging from high-fidelity manikins to emerging virtual reality and artificial intelligence technologies. It explores the diverse modalities used to teach technical and non-technical skills, including Crisis Resource Management and interprofessional teamwork. Furthermore, the article addresses assessment frameworks, such as objective structured clinical examinations, and best practices for debriefing and faculty development. Ultimately, simulation serves to bridge the gap between knowledge and clinical practice.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Neuroradiology: Transforming Diagnosis, Prognostication, and Workflow.
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping neuroimaging across the entirety of the clinical workflow, encompassing patient scheduling, scan quality assurance, image acquisition and reconstruction, automated lesion detection, pathological characterization, treatment planning, and outcome prognostication. This review synthesizes contemporary evidence through a workflow-centric framework, with particular emphasis on AI tools that have achieved real-world clinical implementation. Although reported technical performance across these domains is frequently compelling, critical deficiencies persist in external validation, human-AI benchmarking, model calibration, and standardized performance reporting, collectively impeding full clinical integration. Emerging evidence suggests that the role of the neuroradiologist is transitioning toward a collaborative human-AI paradigm, rather than one of displacement.

title: Large Language Models in the Radiology Workflow: Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted increasing research interest in radiology owing to their capacity for natural language processing and, more recently, multimodal image-text reasoning. This review provides a clinically oriented overview of LLM applications across the radiology workflow, encompassing scan protocols, image interpretation, radiology reporting, and communication with patients and clinicians. Although the existing general-purpose multimodal LLMs show promise in diagnostic tasks, their image-interpretation performance is limited; they often prioritize textual context over visual information, and they are prone to hallucinations. In contrast, LLMs have demonstrated practical utility in radiology reporting, including structured radiology reporting, summarization, automated data extraction, and clinically meaningful report categorization. This review also discusses the reporting guidelines and performance evaluation methodologies specific to LLM research to promote more scientifically rigorous and reproducible studies in this rapidly evolving field. Finally, we outline the future directions for LLM research to support the responsible and effective integration of LLMs in radiology practice. 대형 언어 모델(large language models)은 자연어 처리 능력과 최근의 멀티모달(multimodal) 이미지-텍스트 추론 능력을 바탕으로 영상의학 분야에서 각광을 받고 있다. 본 종설은 영상의학 워크플로우 전반에 걸친 대형 언어 모델의 활용을 임상 중심으로 개괄하며, 검사 프로토콜 결정(scan protocoling), 영상 해석(image interpretation), 판독문 작성(radiology reporting), 그리고 환자 및 임상의와의 의사소통(communication)을 포함한다. 현재 멀티모달 대형 언어 모델은 진단 작업에서 가능성을 보이고 있으나, 영상 해석에서는 신뢰성이 아직까지는 제한적이며 시각 정보보다 텍스트 맥락을 우선적으로 활용하고 환각(hallucination)이 발생하기 쉬운 경향을 보인다. 반면, 판독문 작성 분야에서는 구조화된 판독문 생성(structured radiology reporting), 요약(summarization), 자동 데이터 추출(data extraction), 그리고 판독문 분류(categorization)와 같은 영역에서 실질적인 유용성을 입증하였다. 또한 본 종설에서는 빠르게 발전하고 있는 이 분야에서 보다 과학적으로 엄밀하고 재현 가능한 연구를 촉진하기 위하여, 대형 언어 모델 연구에 특화된 보고 지침(reporting guidelines)과 성능 평가 방법을 논의한다. 마지막으로, 영상의학 임상에서 대형 언어 모델을 책임감 있고 효과적으로 적용하기 위한 향후 발전 방향을 제시한다.

title: Large Language Model Framework for Structured Biomarker Extraction and Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Identification From Pathology Reports: Development and Evaluation Study.
summary: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive molecular subtype of breast cancer that needs to be identified accurately from pathology reports to inform decision-making. Large language models (LLMs) have been reported to show great potential in the automatic extraction of important oncology information from unstructured medical text. We aimed to create and test an LLM-based approach for automatic biomarker extraction and TNBC subtype classification based on breast cancer pathology reports using prompt-engineering techniques. In total, 532 breast cancer pathology reports from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were used. Our approach extracted structured oncology features, such as estrogen receptor status, progesterone receptor status, HER2 status, tumor size, tumor grade, and tumor histology, which were used to identify TNBC. We tested 4 frontier models: GPT-4o mini (released July 18, 2024), GPT-4.1 nano (released April 14, 2025), GPT-5 nano (released August 7, 2025), and Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite. The designed framework was able to extract relevant biomarkers and clinicopathological attributes from unstructured pathology reports and allowed for the automated identification of patients with TNBC. Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite showed superior performance in the extraction of clinicopathological attributes. For all models investigated, chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting was shown to outperform other strategies, such as zero-shot and few-shot prompting, for both biomarker extraction and TNBC classification. GPT-4o mini using CoT prompts reported the highest performance for TNBC classification. Using prompt-engineering techniques based on LLMs proved to be an efficient method of translating unstructured breast cancer pathology reports into structured clinical information. Moreover, it can be used to accurately identify the TNBC subtype.

title: Artificial intelligence in diabetic retinopathy: From deep learning to foundation models, clinical translation, and real-world deployment.
summary: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision impairment worldwide, with its burden increasing in parallel with the global diabetes pandemic. As a progressive microvascular disorder with neurovascular unit involvement, DR is driven by retinal ischemia, inflammation, and pathological neovascularization, while diabetic macular edema (DME) continues to represent a principal cause of vision loss. This structured narrative review provides a critical synthesis of advances in diabetic retinopathy diagnosis, retinal imaging, treatment strategies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening published from January 2020 through March 2026, while selectively incorporating earlier landmark studies to provide clinical and methodological context. We summarize contemporary screening pathways and emerging retinal imaging modalities, including ultra-widefield photography (up to ~200° field of view), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and OCT angiography, examining how complementary structural and vascular biomarkers are reshaping disease severity assessment and DME characterization. We then review the evolution of AI methodologies, highlighting a transition from task-specific convolutional neural network pipelines toward transformer-based and self-supervised representation learning, including retina-specific foundation models designed to reduce annotation burden and improve robustness and generalizability under domain shift. Beyond algorithmic performance on curated benchmarks, we emphasize key translational requirements for clinical adoption, including model calibration, uncertainty-aware triage, image quality control, and external validation across imaging devices and diverse populations. Recent prospective and implementation studies across diverse healthcare systems demonstrate that the real-world effectiveness of AI-enabled DR screening depends not only on diagnostic accuracy but also on image gradability, clinically appropriate operating thresholds, uncertainty management, external validation, referral capacity, and integration with established care pathways. Evidence from the Asia-Pacific region provides important examples of these implementation challenges in heterogeneous and resource-constrained screening environments. Specific attention is given to the identification and mitigation strategies for fundus pigmentation-related performance disparities and the governance of autonomous versus hybrid human-AI screening models within evolving regulatory frameworks. Finally, we examine emerging work in oculomics for systemic risk stratification and propose a pragmatic clinical readiness framework centered on validation hierarchy, safety monitoring, and workflow integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the translational readiness of foundation models, multimodal retinal intelligence, and emerging technologies for large-scale screening, therapeutic decision-making, and longitudinal disease monitoring.

title: Medical superintelligence: foundations and aspirations.
summary: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have stimulated discussions about medical superintelligence, yet how to define and evaluate this aspiration remains unclear. We discuss how AI technologies can contribute to more effective care, introducing six interdependent dimensions of medical intelligence to frame contributions of AI to healthcare delivery. As AI capabilities and their integration into clinical workflows advance, improving the quality of care will require more than superhuman performance on isolated tasks. It will require systems that harness AI, independently and in collaboration with humans, to surpass today's strongest human-led health systems in integrated medical reasoning across the full arc of care. Realising their value will require understanding how these capabilities complement existing medical intelligence and combining them effectively to improve the quality and accessibility of care.

title: AI-driven analysis of genomic alterations in colorectal cancer patients.
The Current Status and Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence in Bladder Cancer: Clinical Applications and Research.
summary: Bladder cancer ranks as the 10th most common malignancy worldwide. Advances in technology are continuously reshaping its diagnosis, treatment selection, and prognosis assessment. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated marked potential in transforming bladder cancer care. By integrating and analyzing multi-source data, AI enhances the precision and efficiency of disease management. This review comprehensively examines the current applications of AI across various domains, including radiographic imaging analysis, pathological diagnosis, cystoscopic image processing, molecular subtyping, drug development, organoid research, prognostic modeling, and medical device innovation. It highlights the advantages of AI over conventional methods, outlines model development strategies, and summarizes commonly employed algorithms. Furthermore, we discuss the key challenges in translating AI tools into real-world clinical practice. This narrative review aims to inform the future development of AI-driven digital health systems, ultimately contributing to the realization of precision medicine and personalized management for bladder cancer patients.

title: Large Language Model-Generated Electronic Consultations: A Blinded Comparative Study of OpenEvidence and Gastroenterologist Electronic Consultations.
summary: To evaluate whether a context-specific large language model, OpenEvidence, can generate gastroenterology/hepatology eConsult responses for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), while characterizing the frequency and potential severity of errors. In this retrospective cohort study at a tertiary academic medical center, 125 specialist electronic consultations (eConsults) for MASLD (from January 2020 to December 2024) were paired with OpenEvidence-generated eConsults produced using OpenEvidence and standardized prompts. Five blinded physician reviewers evaluated all eConsults using a previously validated instrument. A board-certified gastroenterologist independently reviewed OpenEvidence-generated eConsults to identify errors and assess potential for harm. OpenEvidence-generated eConsults received higher overall eConsult Specialist Quality of Response scores than specialist eConsults (mean difference, 6.4; 95% CI, 6.0-6.9; P<.001) and higher global quality ratings (odds ratio [OR], 16.1; 95% CI, 12.0-21.5; P<.001). OpenEvidence-generated eConsults were more likely to be rated as providing an appropriate amount of information (70.9% vs 33.9%; OR, 6.4; 95% CI, 4.8-8.5; P<.001). Of 125 OpenEvidence-generated eConsults, 12 contained minor errors and 1 contained a potentially major error. In this blind comparison of paired eConsults for MASLD, OpenEvidence-generated responses were rated higher in perceived quality and informational adequacy than specialist-authored responses, but occasionally clinically relevant errors occurred. These findings support further evaluation of OpenEvidence-assisted eConsult workflows for protocol-driven conditions.

title: Artificial intelligence models Traditional Chinese Medicine principles to integrate with biomedicine.
summary: Using 26,339 model-eligible Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) formula records, we trained an autoencoder following TCM's compression-expansion logic to learn the TCM embedding space (TCM-ES), quantifying symptom-pattern-formula mappings. TCM-ES aligns with conventional TCM principles not used in training. Biomedical entities were mapped post hoc into the fixed space, supporting formula prediction, retrospective clinical analyses, and exploratory therapeutic prioritization.

title: Toward Precision, Pathogenesis, and Big Data: A New Era in Rheumatic Disease Management.
Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Colposcopy Training Improves Diagnostic Reasoning and Communication Competencies: A Randomized Controlled Study.
summary: Cervical cancer remains a major global health issue, and colposcopy training struggles with standardization and scalability. AI has potential to improve medical education, but its effectiveness in colposcopy training remains underexplored. To evaluate the efficacy of an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven virtual patient platform for colposcopy training among resident physicians. In this randomized, assessor-blinded, wait-list-controlled trial, 60 obstetrics and gynecology residents (PGY-2/3) from two affiliated teaching hospitals were enrolled (May 2023-September 2025). Participants were randomly assigned to either the Immediate AI Intervention group (traditional teaching plus an AI platform throughout) or the Wait-List Control group (traditional teaching only during Month 1, followed by the AI platform). The primary outcome was the between-group difference in the Case Analysis score at 1 month. Secondary outcomes included theoretical knowledge, communication performance, diagnostic justification, and operative competence assessed via OSCE. At 1 month, the Immediate AI group showed superior performance in Case Analysis (78.57 ± 3.72 vs 71.03 ± 5.82, mean difference = 7.54, p<0.001, Cohen's d=1.54), Diagnostic Justification (81.63 ± 6.21 vs 74.13 ± 6.77, p<0.001, Cohen's d=1.15), Communication Performance (80.97 ± 3.90 vs 75.77 ± 6.08, p<0.001, Cohen's d=1.02), and Theoretical Knowledge (84.67 ± 6.27 vs 80.43 ± 5.07, p=0.006, Cohen's d=0.74). Operative competence showed no significant difference (p = 0.113). Both groups achieved high proficiency (over 85 points) within 3 months. Satisfaction was high (90.0% participants, 91.7% supervisors). An AI-driven virtual patient platform significantly accelerates the acquisition of diagnostic reasoning and communication skills in colposcopy training, demonstrating high educational efficacy and acceptance for scalable, standardized education.

title: The Artificial Levite: AI and the Temptation to "Pass By" the Patient.
summary: Healthcare stands to gain much from the integration of artificial intelligence (AI). We must, as a society, decide how it should be ethically implemented into these human-led sectors. After first examining AI from a Catholic perspective at the general scale using Antiqua et Nova, this essay shifts its focus to the implementation of AI in healthcare. With the gaze of the Good Samaritan as a foundation, this essay establishes relational care as a core principle of a Catholic healthcare system that AI threatens to erode. Using the modern incorporation of electronic health records (EHRs) as a parallel, it describes how advancements in technology have dramatically shifted healthcare away from relationality and finally characterizes how the anticipated implementations of AI will likely lead to similar outcomes. Drawing on Antiqua et Nova's distinction between AI that enhances the patient-provider relationship and AI that replaces it, this paper uses the historical adoption of EHRs as a cautionary precedent and examines ambient AI scribes as a test case for what disciplined, relationship-enhancing AI integration can look like.

title: Sequential diagnosis with language models.
summary: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

title: The Differential That Never Gets Generated.
summary: Residents increasingly ask large language models to name a lesion before diagnosing it themselves. The practice contributes a specific harm: never-skilling, a phenomenon in which reasoning is never acquired, and is distinct from 'deskilling' or 'model error'. Forming a differential first is necessary but insufficient. Departments should require documented differentials, supervise disagreement, and examine unassisted reasoning.

title: Vision-Enabled Large Language Models in Mammography: From Benchmarking to Clinical Accountability.
Utilizing the Contrastive Language-Image Pre-Training Model in Chest Radiography: Current Capabilities and Practical Guidance.
summary: Although convolutional neural networks have significantly advanced chest radiography (CXR) analysis, they remain limited in their adaptability to diverse clinical workflows and their interpretability. Recently, contrastive language-image pre-training (CLIP) has emerged as a novel paradigm that enables flexible, zero-shot diagnostic capabilities. Among CLIP-based approaches, Xplainer is particularly noteworthy for its highly customizable prompting framework, which supports diverse queries, even for the same image. However, diagnostic performance may vary substantially depending on the prompt engineering strategy employed. This review outlines the core architecture of CLIP and explores several key CLIP-based applications developed for CXR, focusing particularly on Xplainer, an accessible online tool. We discuss practical considerations, including input image selection, effective prompt engineering strategies (e.g., optimization of prompt structure and content), and performance evaluation approaches. Ultimately, CLIP-based models such as Xplainer represent an important advancement in medical AI by providing frameworks that better align with clinical radiology workflows and support the development of clinician-centered AI systems. 합성곱 신경망(convolutional neural networks)이 흉부 방사선 촬영(chest radiography) 분석을 상당히 발전시켰음에도 불구하고, 종종 사용자 유연성과 해석 가능성 측면에서 한계를 가지고 있다. 최근 대조 언어-이미지 사전 학습 모델(contrastive language-image pre-training; 이하 CLIP)은 영상과 텍스트의 유사도를 기반으로 유연한 제로샷(zero-shot) 진단을 가능하게 하는 새로운 패러다임으로 떠오르고 있다. 다양한 CLIP 기반 접근법 중에서도 Xplainer 모델은 동일한 영상에 대해 다양한 질의를 허용하는 고도의 맞춤형 프롬프트 기능을 갖추고 있어 주목할 만하지만, 이러한 모델은 프롬프트 엔지니어링 전략에 따라 성능이 크게 달라질 수 있는 특징이 있다. 이 연구에서는 CLIP의 핵심 아키텍쳐를 소개하고, 특히 접근성이 뛰어난 온라인 도구인 Xplainer를 중심으로 흉부 방사선 촬영 영상에 특화된 주요 CLIP 기반 어플리케이션들을 소개한다. 또한 입력 이미지 선택, 효과적인 프롬프트 엔지니어링 전략(예: 정상 케이스의 구별, 프롬프트 구조 및 내용 최적화, 질병의 중증도 및 병변 위치 평가), 그리고 성능 평가 방법 등 실질적인 고려 사항들을 논의한다. 궁극적으로 Xplainer와 같은 CLIP 기반 모델은 임상 영상의학에 부합하는 프레임워크를 제공함으로써 의료 AI를 한 단계 발전시키며, 임상의 중심의 AI를 위한 길을 열어줄 것이다.

title: A machine learning-based model for predicting the color of liquid formulation placebos and analyzing their visual similarity.
summary: High-quality randomized, placebo-controlled trials are critical for clinical drug trials, but preparing color‑matched placebos for liquid formulations remains difficult due to the color complexity of liquid formulations and the inefficiency of conventional matching methods. Machine learning offers an effective approach to modeling the complex non-linear relationships among multiple colorants at varying concentrations, enabling prediction of color formulations. This study employed optimal Latin hypercube sampling to generate 253 simulated samples with five colorants. After color correction using a correction matrix, ten color space values were extracted for model fitting. Among five models, random forest (RF) performed best, with a mean absolute error of 0.09, a root mean square error of 0.15, and an R2 value of 0.69. Shapley additive explanations analysis identified L*, G, gray, and V as key variables influencing the prediction of placebo color formulations. Validation against eight target solutions produced average color differences of ΔEab = 3.35 and ΔE00 = 2.20, and a mean visual similarity score of 9.1 by human assessors, indicating a relatively high prediction accuracy. This study developed an RF‑based strategy for predicting the color of placebo in liquid formulations, enabling visual color matching with test drugs in clinical trials.

title: Artificial Intelligence Use Among Health Care Professionals in the United States and United Kingdom: Cross-National Survey.
summary: This cross-sectional study examined AI use among 524 health care professionals in the United States and United Kingdom, focusing on current applications, access, barriers, and factors that could support adoption. AI use was common but varied across professional and national contexts, with findings highlighting the importance of evidence, organizational guidance, training, privacy safeguards, and integration into clinical workflows for responsible adoption.

title: Behavioral and motor deficits following traumatic brain injury: implications for post-traumatic epilepsy.
summary: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) is a severe complication of traumatic brain injury (TBI). Patients with PTE often experience comorbid neurobehavioral deficits, which further reduce the quality of life and impede the recovery of patients. This review examines behavioral and motor deficits associated with PTE across clinical and preclinical studies, with an emphasis on the need to identify PTE-specific phenotypes that may serve as biomarkers of disease development and progression, as well as distinguish PTE from other forms of epilepsy. Despite growing evidence of post-TBI behavioral and motor abnormalities, their relationship with PTE remains unclear, particularly in preclinical models where direct comparisons are limited between animals that do and do not develop PTE. We further evaluate the application of artificial intelligence (AI) for characterizing these phenotypes throughout post-traumatic epileptogenesis, highlighting its potential to provide automated, objective, and sensitive measures of functional outcomes.

title: Machine Learning in Amyloidogenic Polypeptide Research: From Sequence Prediction to Drug Discovery.
summary: Over the past decade, machine learning (ML) has established a transformative paradigm for investigating amyloidogenic polypeptides. Characterized by their propensity to form ordered, β-sheet-rich fibrillar aggregates, these polypeptides are centrally implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD). This review systematically evaluates the application of ML across critical domains of amyloid investigation: sequence-based amyloidogenicity prediction, structural biology, inhibitor design, and amyloid-related clinical objectives. We further summarize the diverse array of ML architectures currently employed in amyloid research, spanning classical algorithms (e.g., support vector machines and random forests) to advanced deep learning frameworks, such as the transformer framework, protein language models (PLMs), etc. Additionally, we spotlight emerging frontiers, namely, the integration of ML with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, the use of generative AI for de novo inhibitor design, etc., while addressing persistent bottlenecks in the field, including data standardization, model interpretability, and rigorous experimental validation for in silico predictions. Ultimately, this review serves as a foundational roadmap for emerging researchers and a definitive reference for established investigators operating at the intersection of artificial intelligence and amyloid biology.
